counterfactual_missing_items: PCR testing showed no evidence of acute or persistent myocardial infection
No raw span identifies a specific infectious trigger
No raw span documents response to immunosuppression
decisive_items: Endomyocardial biopsy revealed moderate chronically active myocarditis with diffuse interstitial remodelling
Coronary angiography revealed no evidence of relevant coronary artery disease
response.rationale: R1 is the only candidate with a tissue-level diagnosis: endomyocardial biopsy shows moderate chronically active myocarditis, directly explaining the acute severe LV failure and cardiogenic shock. R5 matches the echocardiographic distribution (basal/mid akinesia with apical sparing) but is only a suspected phenotype; the biopsy provides the aetiology and supersedes the imaging pattern. R2 and R4 are merely temporal/risk-factor associations and do not account for the biopsy-proven myocardial inflammation.

rejected.why: Only a temporal association with recent surgery; no raw span links the excision to the acute myocardial inflammation or biopsy findings.
Treated arterial hypertension is a chronic risk factor and does not explain the acute cardiogenic shock or biopsy-proven myocarditis.
